## Austin Dental Appointment Request

A morning visit between **2026-07-20 and 2026-07-24** is a good fit for a non-emergency first appointment for mild tooth sensitivity. Below is a polished message you can send, plus a ready-to-use prep list and fee/insurance questions.

## Appointment Request Message and Visit Checklist

**Subject:** Request for New Patient Dental Appointment

Hello,

I’d like to schedule a non-emergency dental appointment for an adult patient in Austin between **July 20 and July 24, 2026**, preferably **in the morning**.

The main concern is **mild tooth sensitivity**. I’m hoping to book an initial visit and would appreciate information about the **new patient exam cost**, any **X-rays or diagnostic fees**, and whether the total initial visit can stay **under $150** if possible.

Please let me know:
- Your earliest available morning appointment in that window
- Whether you accept my insurance, if applicable
- What the estimated first-visit charges would be
- Any forms or records I should bring in advance

Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Best regards,
[Your full name]
[Your phone number]
[Your email]

## What to Have Ready Before You Call or Book

- Full legal name and date of birth
- Phone number and email address
- Preferred appointment dates and morning time range
- Description of symptoms: mild sensitivity, how long it has been happening, and whether it is cold/heat/sweet-related
- Insurance card, if you have dental coverage
- Name of your dental plan and member ID
- Any recent dental records or x-rays, if available
- A list of medications, allergies, and relevant medical conditions
- Preferred pharmacy, if the office asks for it
- Payment method for any copay or self-pay balance

## Questions to Ask About Fees, Insurance, and Follow-Up

- What is the **new patient exam fee**?
- Are **bitewing or full-mouth X-rays** included, or billed separately?
- Is there a **consultation fee** in addition to the exam?
- Can you give me an **estimate for the total first visit** before I come in?
- Do you accept **my insurance plan**?
- Will you **submit claims** directly to insurance?
- What is the **expected copay, deductible, or out-of-pocket amount**?
- If treatment is needed, will you explain the **next-step options and costs** before doing anything?
- If the sensitivity is from a cavity, gum issue, or cracked tooth, what is the **likely follow-up treatment**?
- Do you offer a **payment plan** or self-pay discount if needed?

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Find Dentists] https://www.google.com/maps/search/dentists+in+Austin+TX
Action: [Button: Check Insurance] https://www.ada.org/resources/practice/practice-management/insurance

## Sources

- American Dental Association patient guidance: https://www.ada.org/resources/ada-library/oral-health-topics/tooth-sensitivity
- ADA insurance and practice resources: https://www.ada.org/resources/practice/practice-management/insurance
